sentences.text: Net interest income plus noninterest income rose from $20,956 million in FY2016 to $28,540 million in FY2025, a 3.5% CAGR [D5][D219].
Net interest income compounded at 4.0% and noninterest income at 2.8% over the window [F115][F116].
FY2023 was the step change: revenue rose 15.8% to $28,013 million, driven by higher rates on earning assets and the MUB acquisition, partly offset by deposit mix and pricing [D189][D169][P33].
FY2024 reversed part of that, with revenue down 2.4% to $27,335 million as higher rates pressured deposit mix and pricing [D214][D194][P21].
FY2025 resumed growth, revenue up 4.4% to $28,540 million on loan growth, fixed asset repricing and lower deposit rates [D239][D219][P16].
Payment Services was the steadiest contributor, adding +1.4pp to revenue growth in FY2025 on 5.4% segment growth and a 25.8% share of revenue [D261][D260][D259].
That segment's net revenue rose 5.4% on higher average loan balances, higher loan fees, lower funding costs and higher merchant processing and card revenue [P4].
Consumer and Business Banking shrank, subtracting 1.3pp in FY2025 as segment revenue fell 3.9% and its share slipped to 31.0% [D253][D252][D251].
Its net revenue fell 3.9% on deposit mix changes and second-quarter loan sales, partly offset by higher mortgage banking revenue [P6].
Net income grew 20.2% in FY2025 against 4.4% revenue growth, and EPS rose 21.9% while the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D227][D239][D229][D237].
The efficiency ratio was 59.0% in FY2025, just below its 59.3% window median and well inside the 55.3% low and 67.4% high [D220][D277][D275][D276].
That 59.0% sits below the banks peer median of 61.7%, at the 14th percentile of seven peers [D220][D281][D280].
Noninterest expense fell 2.0% to $16,837 million, reflecting prior-year merger and integration charges, lower compensation and the prior-year FDIC special assessment [D238][X135][P10].
The FY2023 efficiency spike to 67.4% came from a 26.6% expense increase driven by MUB merger and integration charges and a $734 million FDIC special assessment [D170][D188][P30].
The credit-loss provision was 7.7% of revenue in FY2025, above the 6.1% peer median, and the 20.2% effective tax rate kept net margin at 26.5% [D221][D285][D215][D223].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank, so capital return is the better test [F60][F30].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3,657 million in FY2025 covered 48% of net income, down from $6,968 million in FY2019 [D218][F30][D65].
Share repurchases fell to $489 million in FY2025 from $4,525 million in FY2019, while dividends rose to $3,168 million from $2,443 million [X85][X79][X95][X89].
Return on average equity was 12.2% in FY2025, above the 11.8% banks peer median and in the 71st percentile of seven peers [D226][D283][D282].
Loans were 73.5% of deposits, down from 80.5% in FY2016, and the allowance held at 2.0% of loans [D224][D10][D225].
Shareholders' equity rose 11.3% to $65,193 million in FY2025, and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D233][F114][D237].
Long-term debt stood at $39,829 million in FY2022, up 24.0% that year, the last year the pack reports it [F104][D158].
Revenue declined 2.4% in FY2024 to $27,335 million, the one flagged period, driven by higher rates on deposit mix and pricing [R1][D214][D194][P21].
The decline proved short-lived, with revenue up 4.4% in FY2025, so the flag reads as cyclical rather than structural [D239][D219].
The credit-loss provision at 7.7% of revenue sits above the 6.1% peer median, worth watching if credit costs stay elevated [D221][D285].
If the efficiency ratio moves back above the 59.3% window median, the FY2025 cost improvement would be reversing [D220][D277].
If net interest income growth falls below the FY2025 2.2% pace, the loan-growth and repricing tailwind would be fading [D234][F10].
If the credit-loss provision rises above the FY2025 7.7% of revenue, credit quality would be deteriorating against the 6.1% peer median [D221][D285].
